patch_description: The recommendation targets lag_error (0.27) and avg_error (0.29): a single global Q under-serves the 5 Hz component. Instead of estimating Q from the raw denoised input (which mixes measurement noise into the "dynamics"), run the Kalman pass once with a conservative base Q, then estimate per-sample Q from the *smoothed* first-pass output's second differences. Because the smoothed output's d2 contains far less measurement noise, its block-MAD reflects genuine local dynamics. We subtract the expected residual noise floor per block — the residual noise in a window-mean-like estimate scales as σ_r/√w, and second differences amplify it by √6 — then floor at 0.05σ_r and cap at 1.5σ_r, interpolating to per-sample Q[k]. This gives large Q (fast tracking) in genuinely busy segments and small Q (heavy smoothing) in slow segments, directly reducing lag on transients while suppressing spurious reversals elsewhere. σ_r is estimated robustly from the Hampel residual via MAD.
